[quote=lyuongo;61557046][b]VETERAN GENERAL HEIN WEI FIRED BY PRESIDENT, MINING COMPANIES TO BLAME[/b]
[pre][NAYPINAU - 16 MAY 2028] Lyuongo President Tung Aung officially released a statement Tuesday morning officially releasing General Hein Wei from his duties. General Hein cut his teeth in the Lyuongoan Jungle, a hotspot for insurgents and organized crime syndicates alike. The now former General Hein was an adamant opposer to the Lyuongoan Mining Corporation's acquisition of independent mercenary groups in 2019, instead insisting on patrolling the southeast himself. The LMC's board of execs constantly feuded with Hein over the next decade, eventually boiling and crackling last night, ending in a skirmish between the two. As of tonight, 8 are confirmed dead, 12 wounded. Among the dead are 6 of Hein's own men. 

Pressure from interest committees and the military has effectively split the government, with President Tung now thrust in the unfortunate position of having to straddle an unruly military back together. However, one could make the case that this is a better predicament than if the Uranium mining corps turned against him. As Hein heads back to his hometown of Furinau, only time will tell what lies ahead for the Republic.[/pre]

[nation]Lyuongo National Salvation Army[/nation]

 [/quote]
[b]HEIN WEI, FAMED WAR GENERAL TURNED TRAITOR? OR NEW SALVATION FOR LYUONGO?[/b]
[pre][FURINAU - 17 MAY 2028] The news hit General Hein Wei when he reached Furinau. The jungles of Jyuongo had spotty connections at best. In the rain of that dreary city surrounded by his comrades, he was informed via national television that his rank was stripped from him. Fury boiled inside every man present. General Hein Wei had always stood up for them, and now President Tung Aung had tossed him away?! At the urging of his second-in-command, Lieutenant-General Bo Htun, he declared the illegitimacy of the Republic of Lyuongo for siding with the corporations against their own people. Using his senior rank and high level of respect, he would rally approximately half of the Republican Army to his side under the new banner of the National Salvation Army, in the name of Marxist-Leninist-Li'ist-Heinism (a term coined by his underlings; it is not known if Hein himself formally endorses the ideology). 

When rallied, the coup would formally be launched, along the highway leading to Naypinau, the great military convoy would be seen, though even still, several hundred were left behind at Furinau to establish military checkpoints and ensure that their flank could not be broken so easily. News helicopters would fly overhead, documenting the convoys procession to Naypinau, flags bearing the hammer and sickle would be noted in lieu of the flag of the Republic. It was clear to the news reporters that this was not ordinary. Footage would be taken of the pouring rain clouding the trucks, tanks, jeeps and other military vehicles. But even in that haze, orange tips of emblazoned cigarettes could be seen.

The convoy would hit Naypinau like a hammer, and skirmishes would begin across the city between any military targets who did not immediately surrender to the Lyuongo National Salvation Army. Honoured Marshal Hein Wei would be seen fighting amongst his men, giving them a distinct morale boost that the Republican forces would lack. It would be around this time where a portion of the Air Force would defect to Hein's side, along with the entirety of the Navy.[/pre]

It is for the matter of the pursuit of knowledge that many departments of the various prestigious universities of the New Balion Empire have taken upon themselves to launch expeditions to learn, study and share the various unique cultures and peoples out in the world of Erene. It has been noted from various traders and tourists that there are a unique, short-heighted people that apparently live in caves in the rural areas of Irrocco. This has peaked a particular team of anthropologists at the Imperial University of Tandon who have decided upon visiting the country to figure out more. 

A team is ensembled, combined full of anthropologists, ecologists, linguists and other relevant fields of study that will head and visit the nation of Irroco to understand the unique nature of this group. It is led by Dr E. "Indy" Jones with a diplomatic attache led by Sir Boniface Holdstead leading a diplomatic team to help establish formal relations between the Empire and the Islamic state. A small ocean liner is dispatched which takes around 2-3 weeks to reach the seas of Irrocco. It is transmitted through radio that on behalf of Emperor Augustus the 10th, the New Balion Empire wishes to both establish diplomatic relations as well as explore and study various Irroccan peoples.

[nation]Irocco[/nation][/quote]
The Sealiphate of Irocco responds with an open sign of welcoming to the New Balion Empire, and this team assembled to investigate and document the cultures of the world, while privately, the Assembly of Iyaiids is concerned, considering the... northern incident. Nonetheless, the research ship and diplomats are accepted whensoever they arrive in the Sealiphate, largely due to lobbying by the Great Falcon and Old Dove factions, who seek that increasing diplomatic ties amongst even nations sinful will increase the Sealiphate's economic output, and thus allow for the betterment of the lives of the Iroccoan people. Sealiph Ibrahim neglects to meet with any diplomats, unless the Emperor himself is present, and instead delegates that task to his Chancellor. 

As for the research team, Guthurbek Grudgebreaker, Thayn of the Thayndom of Gamlith Drungarth, announces his readiness to accept them into his Thayndom. To understand his people's culture, and for them to understand Balionic culture.

Honório Reis, Dom Honório Reis para ser mais preciso, é um renomado professor na corte imperial, um professor universitário vindo do norte, Jocapá, um homem bem vestido e culto , esforçado, veste preto , usa um terno preto com duas marcas douradas sobre uma camisa branca com uma gola com saliências em forma de espiral nas bordas, e uma gravata azul escura padrão. Ele também usa sapatos de pretos com listras brancas. alto e magro, e com cabelo preto penteado para trás, é uma pode sempre ereta e ajustada, adentrou no quarto de Alteza e fitou o olhar em volta, pegou debaixo de seu terno um livro, e então encostou no ombro do príncipe herdeiro, Dom Leonardo que estava parado, olhando a janela.
"Vossa alteza, hoje, aprenderemos mais que simples figuras [i]de fora.[/i]"
O tutor começou dizendo, Leo se virou e sorriu, e estendendo a mão para o livro que lhe era oferecido:
"Clóvis Barbosa[i], O dever do estado.[/i]"
Um autor sulista, nascido na época oligárquica ha mais de 100 anos, cujas obras hoje são publicadas por fundações em seu nome e seu material é publicado em materiais didáticos por boa parte do país, suas obras e sua vida são muito comuns de serem encontradas, afinal um pensador dedicado teria suas obras preservadas.
O garoto leu em voz alta, tateando a capa. mas , o tutor deu um olhar de desaprovação, ele pegou o livro e o abriu:
"Livros fechados são livros mortos."
Apontou para uma seção em específico:
[i]O cidadão comum, exausto de lutar contra estruturas que não compreende por completo, acaba por aceitar sua condição não como imposição, mas como destino. E é nesse ponto que o sistema atinge sua forma mais perigosa: quando deixa de ser percebido como sistema.
[/i]
"Lhe soa familiar?"
Honório perguntou, logo Leo respondeu:

Honório observou atentamente,talvez até uma pitada de admiração não dita pelas palavras do menino.

Ele repetiu o lema nacional, vendo a ironia da situação , antes de prosseguir
"Alteza...já ouviu sobre...Passado dos Presentes, de Rodrigo Sá?"

[spoiler=The Orchestrator]

King Zachariasz rose from his slumber. He sat up slowly, looking outside the large glass window. The night, blacker than black, shrouded the courtyard with a mantle of mystery that had once entangled the land and now seemed reborn. At his side was his wife, the queen. The king stood slowly, careful not to wake her, as he proceeded to leave his bed. He cloaked himself with his royal robe bedight with innumerable scales of gold and placed a crimson belt around his waist that held his blade and scabbard.

He walked through the corridors of the palace whilst resting his hand on the hilt of his blade, and the guards stood tall as he passed them by. The king passed through the corridors, overlooking the darkened panes of stained glass with depictions of heroism done by his people in the centuries past, through the courtyard with the multitude of flowers, and into a room reserved for his use. The guards before the double doors stepped aside and opened them to him, and Zachariasz entered, taking a seat at the velvet bench seat and placing his hands upon the harpsichord. He ran his fingers over the wooden keys before he began to play.

  

[/spoiler]

[i]Bach Concerto No.1 in D Minor BWV 1052[/i]

[spoiler=The Confines of the Empire & the Meskalamet Tribe]

There was great beauty in the virgin lands that lied to the West, seemingly untouched by the civilizations of old and teeming with the songs of nature; there was greater beauty yet in what it would become.

Chancellor Radziwiłł stood at the frontier of the Empire. Accompanying him was a specialized exploration group consisting of fifty men armed with Imperial rifles. This was the survey team. The group departed from the City-State-Cluster sector of the Empire under orders of the king in order to find the most optimal place for the Empire to spread its borders to. There was myriad resources to be found, but the direction had to be chosen wisely.

[i]"Here,"[/i] said the Chancellor to those who followed him, [i]"is where the king has placed his trust in us. We must not let him down."[/i]

His men nodded.

Soon, they were off to survey the land for resources and find where in the area of Elesyr the Empire was to expand next.

  

The Chancellor and the men that the king had appointed boarded infantry fighting vehicles manufactured in the Drakhalian industry sector and took off. The rumble of the engines spread throughout the silent lands as the formation advanced.

[i]"Sir,"[/i] began one of the soldiers seated next to the Chancellor, [i]"these lands are rumored to belong to a fierce people."[/i]

The Chancellor smiled. [i]"We are also a fierce people. Do you not remember all that we have done to subjugate the C.S.C sector that now belongs to us and us alone? Or what we have done to those that stood against us in the [b]Windspielnacht?[/b]"[/i]

The soldier shook his head. [i]"These are a different kind. I think we should move carefully."[/i]

[i]"I'll keep that in mind."[/i] He did, in fact, not keep that in mind.



At the third hour of their journey, the entourage had stopped by the base of a low hill and was analyzing the composition of the soil for minerals and valuable resources when the first of the figures on horseback appeared. A glint of light from a crude binocular flashed from across the prairie, and the rider was gone. Few men saw the phenomenon, and even fewer spoke of it.

The fourth hour came, and the Sun was high in the sky. The men rested in a valley, when suddenly the sounds of war cries broke out through the tops of the hills that surrounded them.

Quickly, the Chancellor and his men took hold of their rifles, and the gunners on the infantry fighting vehicles took aim; the aggressors would not be given time to rectify their error. They fired upon the approaching riders. Some fell from their mounts and tumbled to the ground, but others were unfazed, and others yet were gone from view when the trigger was pulled.

The tribe of Meskalamet was now upon them. Perhaps it was luck, or perhaps it was God's grace, but as the devils on horseback approached with their chanting and let loose a hail of arrows, the Chancellor closed the door to his vehicle, and the hoop iron point that would have punctured his neck was now shattered like glass upon the steel of the vehicle. A dent formed on the other side of the door.

As the tribesmen continued their rapid advance, all the Corzerraneans were within their vehicles, and now began to fire upon them. Many tribesmen were hit and fell dead on the ground, but they responded with a volley of their own. Every time a tribesman would release an arrow he said a short sentence in a foreign tongue, and the air vibrated with power. The strength increased, and the arrows fired began to pierce through the outer armor of the infantry fighting vehicles. The fighting continued until one of the arrows hit the vehicle in which the Chancellor was it and pierced through it, bringing in spall into the inner compartment.

The Chancellor, still alive, shouted an order. [i]"Fall back!"[/i]

Thus the retreat back a couple miles began, and the tribe of Meskalamet pursued for a portion of the distance before going back to collect their dead.

[/spoiler]

[spoiler=Black Hand Intervention]

Director Johann Karl Tötentod arrived with a squadron of twenty men. They rode in black vehicles of mysterious make forged in the underground facilities of the Empire. The Chancellor met with him at the border regions of Drakhalia and the unclaimed land.

[i]"Director,"[/i] said he, [i]"the Meskalamites are savages. They wield powers that the world has never seen. How could it be that a man on horseback with nothing but primitive weaponry would be able to pierce through the armor of the modern machines of war?"[/i]

The Director knowingly shook his head. [i]"The tribe of Meskalamet holds some special knowledge over a science that they call their own. You are not at fault for not knowing, the scope of this assignment was beyond your capabilities. You did right to call on the king."[/i]

With that, the Director left the Chancellor and began to lead the new squadron of the Black Hand. The Chancellor followed, his own men sharing his curiosity. They watched as the sleek machines of war sliced through the open plains and approached their targets.

Again the tribesmen appeared, and began to fire their charged arrows at the advancing Corzerraneans. One of the machines, built like a tank, pointed its barrel towards the tribesmen, and a strange noise began to emanate from its engine. The hail of arrows were reduced to broken wooden sticks and iron points as they came into contact with the black hull of the machinery. The operatives of the Black Hand continued forward and pushed back the ranks of the tribe of Meskalamet. The Chancellor watched as the tribesmen were made powerless.

After the advance had continued for several miles, the entourage halted, and the Director exited his vehicle. The Chancellor followed.

[i]"Continue your surveying,"[/i] said the Director, [i]"and we will stay here with you until it is complete."[/i]

The Chancellor nodded, not fully understanding what the Black Hand has done but choosing to faithfully continue his service to the task the king has given him.

[/spoiler]

[spoiler=

[pre]Czarny[/pre]]

King Zachariasz arrived at the frontier with his royal entourage after the task had been completed, now fully dressed in his royal garb. The Chancellor greeted him when he arrived.

[i]"Greetings, my liege,"[/i] he began, [i]"I've completed the work you've assigned me over the course of the last few weeks."[/i] The Chancellor handed the King some documents

The King looked over the files. [i]"You have done very well. In your report, you state there to be an abundance of coal in this area. Have you yet laid the details on how the transportation of personnel and equipment will be made in order to not interfere with the proposed mining locations?"[/i]

The Chancellor nodded. [i]"Indeed I have. There is a stretch of land with less resources than the other places, which may be a location for us to build a town or city for the people who would come here for work. We may then build a railway to that city from the border of Drakhalia or Iskra, whichever sector you prefer, which can be rerouted rather easily."[/i]

[i]"Thank you for your faithful service. You are dismissed. There is a flight for you in Drakhalia to return to the capital city of the nation."[/i]

The Chancellor nodded once again, and took his leave.

The King looked over the documents one last time. [i]"I will name this sector [b]Czarny[/b], for from it I will mine black coal."[/i]

[/spoiler]

[pre]Aurestia[/pre]]

Queen Szkarłat had just met with the Nexite Church Council. One thing was abundantly clear: the Church needed space. A lot of it.

During the prior years the Church had filled repositories of knowledge throughout the Empire, and many of these places had hosted universities sponsored by the Church. The Nexites had no issue with the arrangement, and believed it to be in their best interest as well as the people of Corzerran's. However, there was now another issue: there were new innovations to be made, and the Church, having dedicated the majority of its buildings to respositories of knowledge, could not have enough space to continue its pioneering into new areas of science without shutting down some places where students were taught. There would also need to be collaboration with certain corporations, namely Ciernokraj Research Frontier and Corvexa Electronics.

There was also the issue of expanding the coast. There was something that the King had told Szkarłat earlier: it was in the best interest of the Empire to get a larger coastline for better freedom. In the current state, the Empire of Corzerran was very restricted, and only had a few ports from which merchant and military ships could dock at and depart from.

Knowing these two facts, Queen Szkarłat went off to the Northeast to see the land for herself.



There were many guards surrounding the Queen as she exited the black vehicle. She was advised quite extensively against taking this journey and was told that another would gladly do it in her stead, but she decided that it would be best for her to leave the palace for a small break from her queenly duties.

There were tall mountains more inland, and the area near the coast was nearly flat. The mountains were not the best terrain, but she knew that they meant there were resources to be found in abundance. The flatland, though, was what she was more interested in. It stretched far beyond what her eyes could see, and she imagined that the ground was firm and a strong foundation. There could be not only research stations built here, but also many cities and factories. This land was full of opportunity.

Upon seeing this, she returned back to Solaria, where she knew that her husband would be awaiting her return.



Approximately a few days later, King Zachariasz went for himself to look at the land that his wife had proposed to him. He knew of the general features of the land. He had previously thought that expanding in one direction may already place too much strain on the Corzerranean economy for a simultaneous expansion, but during his time in the palace he had checked over several numbers on the economy and saw that the Empire was ready. The land could be developed once it was in his possession, but obtaining the land first is what was important.

The King was accompanied by many members of the Royal Guard and prospectors to analyze the resources available. It was found that within the mountains there were large amounts of copper and iron, both of which would be valuable materials for the Empire's future. Several plans were made in the following days that they stayed in this location, each with varying levels of urbanization, militarization, and ports both merchant and military. After some time, King Zachariasz looked over the finished proposals, and chose to put together a new one that would combine several elements. There was to be an urban area closer to the current borders of the nation, and further out there was to be an industrial center. The industrial center would be placed near the mountains in order to facilitate the transportation of extracted resources directly to the refineries.

This would result in two sectors, which would be named [b]Aurestia[/b] and [b]Pyłowiec[/b], for the urbanized area and for the industrial sector.

Now came the city planning. King Zachariasz saw Aurestia almost as a second Arrin Mounts sector: there was much trade to be had through there, and the amount of urbanization would be very high. However, since it lied between two other sectors and the ocean, the space available would need to be planned out. This needed to be done with the consideration of all possible parties, so the King called forth a representative from each party that he considered important for the loaning of land. There was the Nexite Church, TITAN Industrial Works, ORION Mining Corporation, Ciernokraj Research Frontier, and Corvexa Electronics.

The meeting went smoothly, and went as expected. ORION Mining Corporation went first and put a claim for the land near the mountains that held high amounts of iron and copper ore, and TITAN Industrial Works followed soon after and selected the lands directly or nearly adjascent to theirs. Corvexa Electronics planned to have their buildings in the urban Aurelia, somewhat distanced from the other corporations that claimed lands prior to it, but it chose places within the cities that were closest to the claims of ORION Mining Corporation and TITAN Industrial Works. Ciernokraj Research Frontier chose bulidings that were closer to the center of the city, since they did not require so much ease of transport of raw or manufactured materials but rather were more interested in ease of employee transport. They selected some locations near the residential zones that were not already occupied by planned public parks or other amenities. Then, the Nexite Church selected their locations. The Church selected some locations at the hearts of certain cities, but also put a claim to place a few large installations by the edges of the urban areas. These large installations were meant to be the new research sites for the Church.

After the other representatives had left, the one for the Nexite Church stayed behind to speak with the King. The reason why the large research installation was necessary was because the Nexite Church was planning to start up research on the magic native to the soil of Corzerran again. This was a project that had been abandoned since early 2003 due to other things being requried. However, now that the Nexite Church had helped with the universities of the Empire, they once again needed to seek ways to increase their collective knowledge. The Corzerranean King accepted the Nexite proposal, but only under one condition: the results of the research done regarding magic be sent to the King for review, where it would go into the hands of some of his staff. This pained the representative, but he obliged and accepted the condition.

Finally, once alone, the King reviewed the claims and revised some parts of the plans to better improve the efficiency of the two new sectors. After he looked over it briefly once more, he had a meeting with several city planners, who evaluated the final product. They revised some portions of the plans, and after some time the plans were finalized.

Upon the finalization of the city plans, King Zachariasz went once more to the lands that would become Aurelia and Pyłowiec. There was some beauty in the natural landscape, but it would need to change for the betterment of the Empire. If the circumstances allowed, he thought to himself, there would be some natural conservation areas designated into these lands both for the enjoyment of the people and for the preservation of the ecology.

[pre][FURINAU - 17 MAY 2028] The news hit General Hein Wei when he reached Furinau. The jungles of Jyuongo had spotty connections at best. In the rain of that dreary city surrounded by his comrades, he was informed via national television that his rank was stripped from him. Fury boiled inside every man present. General Hein Wei had always stood up for them, and now President Tung Aung had tossed him away?! At the urging of his second-in-command, Lieutenant-General Bo Htun, he declared the illegitimacy of the Republic of Lyuongo for siding with the corporations against their own people. Using his senior rank and high level of respect, he would rally approximately half of the Republican Army to his side under the new banner of the National Salvation Army, in the name of Marxist-Leninist-Li'ist-Heinism (a term coined by his underlings; it is not known if Hein himself formally endorses the ideology). 

When rallied, the coup would formally be launched, along the highway leading to Naypinau, the great military convoy would be seen, though even still, several hundred were left behind at Furinau to establish military checkpoints and ensure that their flank could not be broken so easily. News helicopters would fly overhead, documenting the convoys procession to Naypinau, flags bearing the hammer and sickle would be noted in lieu of the flag of the Republic. It was clear to the news reporters that this was not ordinary. Footage would be taken of the pouring rain clouding the trucks, tanks, jeeps and other military vehicles. But even in that haze, orange tips of emblazoned cigarettes could be seen.

The convoy would hit Naypinau like a hammer, and skirmishes would begin across the city between any military targets who did not immediately surrender to the Lyuongo National Salvation Army. Honoured Marshal Hein Wei would be seen fighting amongst his men, giving them a distinct morale boost that the Republican forces would lack. It would be around this time where a portion of the Air Force would defect to Hein's side, along with the entirety of the Navy.[/pre][/quote]

[i]President Tung took one last look around the Presidential Palace. It was quiet, bar the helicopter idiling on the roof, awating his appearance. 

Just miles to the south, on the National Highway, the roar of revolution reverberated through the Lyuongoan countryside. Thousands of men, trucks and the red spirit were on a collision course to the capital. Tung ordered the preparation of defenses along the ancient city quarters, however, he knew it was only a matter of time. The remaining troops in Naypinau were to flee to the major port city of Uria, while the rest of the remaining loyalists were to report to command stations in Durgo, Jayunggi and Ryuloga. It would be best now to take stock and prepare their counterattack when the LNA could pick the board in which the final game will be played. Various LMC-employed militias have also pledged loyalty towards the LNA... but you can't exactly rely on mercenaries to be ride or die allies. Tung knew that.

"Your execllency. It's time, we have to go now before the LNSA can get their jets sortied!"

The rain came down in sheets. Fighting in the Naypinau streets were marked with blurred flashes and bangs, but the hundreds of bodies that now lay dead and disfigured in the wet pavement are gracefully covered by the fog of the rain, which washes blood, guts and limbs down the street gutters. Tanks, covered by the fog, trampled mercilessly over friend and foe alike in the confusion. Artillery hit about as many belligerents as it hit civilians. The song of smoke, fog and fire rang out to both the damned and the innocent that night. Even still, the LNSA pushed on, rallied by the great national hero. By the time the sun rose in the morning to shine over the wounded and dead, the LNSA cut off any exits from Naypinau for the remaining loyalists, and from there, it was shooting fish in a barrel. The remaining massacre would last deep into the 18th of May, as the remaining souls of the loyalists would be vanquished with an revolutionary exorcism of the city, regressed to a morbid mass grave covered in bits of pieces of rubble and human matter. In  the meantime, sandbags and barbed wire defenses were being prepared around the perimeter of Uria, with the knowledge that for the LNA to recieve the support it needs for its counterattack, [b]Operation 5692[/b], they had to hold the city of Uria for as long as possible. A job placed into the hands of decades-old tanks and a few thousand men with the resolve of a nation on their backs. They would need every little bit of that resolve, as the Navy, now in Hein Wei's hands, has cut off their escape. They must fight long enough for victory or die waiting for a savior.[/i]
